🚀 Microsoft is increasingly using its own MAI models for everyday Copilot tasks, while reserving OpenAI and Anthropic models for more complex requests.

Microsoft pays Anthropic and OpenAI billions. Now it's quietly trying to stop.

Microsoft has started routing a meaningful share of Excel and Outlook Copilot prompts away from OpenAI and Anthropic to its own in-house MAI models — and it's happening faster than most people realize.

What's actually going on:

 → Tens of thousands of AI prompts per week in Excel and Outlook now run on Microsoft's own MAI models
 → These handle the everyday stuff — summarizing emails, drafting replies, formatting sheets
 → OpenAI's frontier models still power the harder, complex tasks — this isn't a full breakup

So Microsoft is doing what any company with enough scale eventually does: building its own version of the thing it's paying someone else for.

It's a familiar playbook — Amazon did it with AWS chips, Apple did it with silicon. Now it's happening with AI models, right inside the tools millions of us use every day.

The uncomfortable question for users: if the model swap is about cutting Microsoft's costs, not improving your experience, are you the one who ends up with a downgrade?

Researchers built MedCalc-Pro to test how LLMs handle complex medical calculations. The benchmark includes 2,268 real clinical cases across 77 calculators. Unlike existing tests, it requires multi tool reasoning and nested calculations that mirror actual clinical work.

external.description: Current benchmarks for evaluating large language models (LLMs) in medical calculation are largely based on simplified settings, where each patient case corresponds to a single calculator and the required tool is explicitly specified in the query. However, real clinical scenarios often require multiple calculators for joint evaluation, nested-scale calculation, and fuzzy queries that do not directly specify the target calculator. To this end, we propose a new medical calculation benchmark, MedCalc-Pro, which covers three progressively challenging task settings: single-calculator, multi-calculator, and nested-calculator calculation settings. MedCalc-Pro contains 2,268 real-world clinical cases, covering 77 medical calculators across 14 clinical departments. Meanwhile, to address the limited performance of existing frameworks and methods in complex clinical scenarios, we further propose a more generalizable agent framework that supports multi-tool selection and nested-tool calling, while suppressing parameter error propagation through structured validation and evidence review. We conduct systematic comparisons across open-source, closed-source, and medical-specialized LLMs, and the results show that our framework achieves the best performance across all three task settings. This work provides a new benchmark and method for evaluating and applying LLMs in challenging medical calculation scenarios.
external.title: MedCalc-Pro: Solving Complex Medical Calculations with LLM Agents

Hi everyone,

I am writing this to bring light to a critical, long-standing, and frankly anti-consumer backend logic flaw in OpenAI’s iOS App Store In-App Purchase (IAP) verification system.

### The Issue

I recently subscribed to ChatGPT Plus on my current active OpenAI account via the iOS app. Apple successfully processed the payment (Order ID: **MT8ZQ8QJJW**), verified my Apple ID, and transmitted the transaction signal. However, my current active account remains stuck on the Free plan, and clicking ‘Restore Purchases’ returns a persistent error.

### The Root Cause (Database Deadlock)

After escalating this with both Apple Senior Advisors and OpenAI Support (Ticket handled by Marc Brian), OpenAI confirmed that they successfully traced the payment but **misrouted the Plus entitlements** to a legacy, permanently abandoned, and long-expired OpenAI account that I used years ago.

This happens because OpenAI’s receipt-validation system hard-locks an Apple ID to the _very first_ OpenAI account it ever interacted with based on the `Original Transaction ID`. Even if that legacy account’s subscription expired ages ago, OpenAI’s backend stubbornly refuses to route new purchases to a newly logged-in account under the same Apple ID.

### Why This Architecture is Broken

  1. **Contradicts Normal Commercial Logic:** Coming over from Claude (Anthropic), their IAP system treats the Apple ID as a flexible wallet—whoever is currently logged into the app gets the premium features. OpenAI, however, uses it as a rigid identity binder.
  2. **Support is Tech-Incapable/Policy-Blocked:** OpenAI Support explicitly stated in their email: _“Our current policies do not permit unlinking an Apple ID from an existing OpenAI account… Unfortunately, we are unable to manually transfer or reassign a subscription.”_
  3. **Absurd Workarounds:** Support literally suggested that I should “create a brand new Apple ID” just to bypass OpenAI’s poorly written backend architecture.



### Call to Action

This is a massive oversight in system architecture. As consumers, if our legacy accounts are abandoned or lost, our Apple IDs are essentially “bricked” from ever purchasing ChatGPT Plus on iOS again.

OpenAI Engineering team: **Please open a backend tool or workflow for your Tier-1/Tier-2 support staff to manually clear or wipe the`Original Transaction ID` / Apple ID bindings from database records when a user requests it.** Taking a customer’s money via Apple and refusing to deliver the service due to a rigid database lock is entirely unacceptable.

Has anyone else successfully forced a backend manual override for this, or is a forced Apple chargeback the only way out?
external.title: Critical IAP Deadlock: Apple ID Hard-locked to Abandoned Account, Blocking Plus Provisioning for New Accounts
